headline: Resilient Japan battle back twice to draw 2-2 with Netherlands in Texas thriller
summary: Japan secured a dramatic point in World Cup Group F after a late equalizer saved them from defeat against the Netherlands.
details: Japan fought back twice from behind to secure a 2-2 draw against the Netherlands in a high-intensity World Cup Group F match held in Texas.
The first half remained goalless as Japan's compact defending frustrated the Dutch side throughout the opening 45 minutes.
The deadlock broke in the 51st minute when Virgil van Dijk headed in a cross from Ryan Gravenberch to give the Netherlands an early second-half lead.
Japan responded quickly, leveling the score six minutes later through a fierce low shot from outside the area by Keito Nakamura.
The Netherlands regained the lead in the 64th minute after a brilliant strike by Crysencio Summerville hit the far post and went in.
In a dramatic finish, substitute Koki Ogawa scored a superb header from a corner just two minutes before full-time to ensure the draw.
The Netherlands will next face Sweden in Houston, while Japan is scheduled to play Tunisia in Monterrey on June 20.
caption:
Two goals down, twice they fought back! Japan secures a dramatic 2-2 draw against the Netherlands in a Texas thriller.

Japan fought back twice from behind to secure a 2-2 draw against the Netherlands in a high-intensity World Cup Group F match held in Texas.

The first half remained goalless as Japan's compact defending frustrated the Dutch side throughout the opening 45 minutes.

The deadlock broke in the 51st minute when Virgil van Dijk headed in a cross from Ryan Gravenberch to give the Netherlands an early second-half lead.

Japan responded quickly, leveling the score six minutes later through a fierce low shot from outside the area by Keito Nakamura.

The Netherlands regained the lead in the 64th minute after a brilliant strike by Crysencio Summerville hit the far post and went in.

In a dramatic finish, substitute Koki Ogawa scored a superb header from a corner just two minutes before full-time to ensure the draw.

The Netherlands will next face Sweden in Houston, while Japan is scheduled to play Tunisia in Monterrey on June 20.

headline: 10 businesses fined for waste disposal in Shahbag own clean-up drive
summary: The State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives led a sudden 'clean-up drive' in Shahbag, targeting illegal waste dumping.
details: The State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives conducted a surprise 'clean-up drive' in the Shahbag area of Dhaka immediately after the parliamentary session ended.
During the operation, the minister personally inspected the streets and identified several businesses that were illegally dumping waste on the roads.
As a result of the drive, 10 business owners were fined on the spot for violating waste disposal regulations.
The minister emphasized that keeping the city clean is a collective responsibility and warned that strict action will be taken against those who pollute the public spaces.
This sudden move is part of a broader effort to improve urban sanitation and enforce environmental laws in the capital city.
caption:
10 businesses fined on the spot! A State Minister leads a surprise clean-up drive in Shahbag.

The State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives conducted a surprise 'clean-up drive' in the Shahbag area of Dhaka immediately after the parliamentary session ended.

During the operation, the minister personally inspected the streets and identified several businesses that were illegally dumping waste on the roads.

As a result of the drive, 10 business owners were fined on the spot for violating waste disposal regulations.

The minister emphasized that keeping the city clean is a collective responsibility and warned that strict action will be taken against those who pollute the public spaces.

This sudden move is part of a broader effort to improve urban sanitation and enforce environmental laws in the capital city.
